stemMd: How many real solutions does |2x − 1| = 5 have?
explanationMd: Set 2x − 1 equal to 5 or −5. The solutions are x = 3 and x = −2, and both satisfy the original equation. There are exactly two because each linear case has one solution.

distractorRationale.b: Both sign cases produce valid real values.
distractorRationale.c: An absolute-value equation with a positive right side normally has two linear sign cases.
distractorRationale.a: There are only two sign cases for this linear expression.
distractorRationale.e: The equation restricts x to two isolated values.
